findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Do not materialize the result: read the rows through a database cursor (or keyset pages on created_at, id) and stream each CSV line to the response, honouring backpressure. Cost is then constant in memory instead of linear in the organization's history. If a bound is preferred (e.g. a date range per request), that changes the spec and must be decided there.
findings.title: The export loads the whole audit log of an organization into memory

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Write the CSV line by line to a stream (e.g. a Transform from the cursor to the response) so the work is split across event-loop turns, and no second copy of the data (lines array plus joined string) is allocated.
findings.title: Building the whole CSV string blocks the event loop

findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Check with EXPLAIN that an index on (org_id, created_at) exists, or add it to the plan; otherwise the database sorts the organization's rows on every export.
findings.title: No index is planned for the filter and sort of the export query

findings.evidence: `GET /admin/audit-events.csv` SHALL return every audit event of the organization as CSV, oldest first.
findings.location: specs/audit-export/spec.md#Requirement: Administrators export the audit log
findings.recommendation: State how the export stays bounded in resources: either a streamed response (memory independent of the number of events) with a scenario covering a large organization, or an explicit range or page parameter. Add a task that measures the export on a realistic volume (millions of rows).
findings.title: The spec requires an unbounded export with no performance criterion
